$schema-comment: Tier 2 structured exception registry. Each exception must have: id, summary, rationale, expires (YYYY-MM-DD), approvedBy, approvedOn. Audits cite IDs in 'Accepted Risks'. Expired entries fail CI. See .security/audits/README.md for format details.

exceptions.summary: Single maintainer — no separation of duties
exceptions.rationale: This project is maintained by a single developer (Ryan Armstrong). There is no second maintainer available to serve as an independent release approver. The AI assistant (via security-audit-system skill) assists with authoring, review, and security audit, but this does not constitute true separation of duties as the same person (Ryan) directs the AI and holds final sign-off authority. This exception acknowledges the risk that a single compromised account or malicious insider could bypass review. Mitigation: all changes are public on GitHub, releases are cryptographically attested by GitHub Actions (SLSA L2), and the audit trail is publicly verifiable. This exception should be reviewed and removed if/when a second trusted maintainer joins the project.

exceptions.summary: ExcelJS 4.4.0 transitive CVEs in Node-only code paths
exceptions.rationale: ExcelJS 4.4.0 has known transitive vulnerabilities in glob, archiver, brace-expansion, and inflight (e.g., CVE-2025-64756). These vulnerabilities exist in Node.js-only code paths used by workbook.xlsx.write() and similar APIs. This application only calls workbook.xlsx.load(buffer) in the browser UMD bundle (src/components/ImportModal.js), where those Node-only modules are not executed. The risk is effectively zero in the current browser-only configuration. Enterprise scanners pointed at the SBOM may flag these transitive dependencies; this exception documents that the vulnerable code paths are unreachable.
